title: This Parasite Eats a Fish's Tongue, Then Becomes the Tongue
subject: tongue-eating louse

scenes.text: Some fish have a living animal where their tongue should be.
It starts as a tiny swimmer that slips in through the gills and crawls into the mouth.
Then it grips the tongue with sharp legs and cuts off its blood supply. The tongue withers and falls off.
The parasite clamps onto the stump and takes over. It feeds on the fish's blood and mucus.
Scientists call it the only known parasite that functionally replaces an organ of its host.
And the fish often lives on for years, chewing with a tongue that is alive and not its own.

description:
Some fish have a living animal where their tongue should be.
The tongue-eating louse cuts off the tongue's blood supply, then attaches to the stump and takes its place.
Would you have believed it? Tell us below.
first_comment: Fish with this parasite can live for years. Which animal would you least want as a lodger?
